source.title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics

accepted.question_text: Let f be a holomorphic local dynamical system fixing a point p on a complex manifold M, and let K_f = ⋂_{k≥0} f^{-k}(U) be its stable set in a sufficiently small neighborhood U of p. What is the local topological structure of the germ of K_f at p? In particular, must K_f have non-empty interior, be locally connected at p, have K_f \ {p} connected, or impose specific homological or cohomological structure on U \ K_f near p?

evidence.quote: (Q1) What is the topological structure of (the germ at p of ) Kf ? For instance, does Kf have non-empty interior? Is it locally connected at p? Is Kf \ {p} connected? What is the topological (homological, cohomological) structure of U \ Kf ?

accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic local dynamical system f with stable set K_f, what is the dynamical structure of the induced global system (K_f, f)? More specifically, how do orbits in K_f behave asymptotically near the fixed point, can they converge or exhibit chaotic behavior, can there be dense orbits, and what proper forward-invariant subsets of K_f can occur together with their internal dynamics?

evidence.quote: (Q2) What is the dynamical structure of (Kf , f)? For instance, what is the asymptotic behavior of the orbits? Do they converge to p, or have they a chaotic behavior? Is there a dense orbit? Do there exist proper f-invariant subsets...?

accepted.question_text: For holomorphic local dynamical systems at a fixed point in an n-dimensional complex manifold, find a class F of normal forms, preferably small, such that every system is locally conjugate to a possibly unique element of F under holomorphic, smooth, C^k, or topological conjugacy. In other words, can one classify these systems by explicit normal forms within each regularity category?

evidence.quote: (Q3) Find a (possibly small) class F of holomorphic local dynamical systems at O ∈ C^n such that every holomorphic local dynamical system ... is holomorphically (respectively, smoothly, C^k, or topologically) locally conjugated to a (possibly) unique element of F...

accepted.question_text: Associate computable invariants, ideally from a small class, to each holomorphic local dynamical system at the origin of C^n so that equality of invariants characterizes conjugacy as strongly as possible. In particular, can one construct complete invariant systems for holomorphic, smooth, C^k, or topological local conjugacy classes?

evidence.quote: (Q4) Find a way to associate a (possibly small) class of (possibly computable) objects, called invariants, to any holomorphic local dynamical system f ... The class of invariants is complete if two holomorphic local dynamical systems ... are ... locally conjugated if and only if they have the same invariants.

accepted.question_text: For holomorphic local dynamical systems at the origin of C^n, determine normal forms and complete invariants for the weaker equivalence relation of formal conjugacy, where maps are compared up to invertible formal power-series changes of coordinates rather than convergent holomorphic ones.

evidence.quote: (Q5) Find normal forms and invariants with respect to the relation of formal conjugacy for holomorphic local dynamical systems at O ∈ C^n.

accepted.question_text: Find natural families of one-variable elliptic holomorphic germs of the form f_{λ,a}(z)=λz+z^2 g_a(z), parametrized by a in some parameter space M, for which holomorphic linearizability is equivalent exactly to the Brjuno condition on the multiplier λ. In particular, is every elliptic polynomial, or even every elliptic cubic polynomial, holomorphically linearizable if and only if its multiplier is a Brjuno number?

evidence.quote: (OP1) Find families {fλ,a(z) = λz+z^2ga(z)}a∈M ⊂ End(C, O) of elliptic discrete holomorphic dynamical systems such that fλ,a is holomorphically linearizable if and only if λ is a Brjuno number. For instance, is it true that an elliptic polynomial ... or ... an elliptic cubic polynomial ... ?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the Brjuno function on irrational angles and let r(θ) denote the infimum of the radii of convergence of linearizations for injective holomorphic germs on the unit disk with multiplier e^{2πiθ}. Does the function log r(θ) + B(θ) extend from irrational θ to all of [0,1) as a 1/2-Hölder continuous function?

evidence.quote: (OP2) Does log r + B admit a 1/2-Hölder continuous extension to [0, 1)?

accepted.question_text: For one-variable elliptic holomorphic germs with a Cremer fixed point at the origin, are two topological invariants sufficient for complete topological classification: the multiplier f'(0) and the homeomorphism class of the stable set germ K_f at the origin? Equivalently, do those two data completely determine the topological local conjugacy class of a Cremer point?

evidence.quote: (OP3) Are the multiplier and the homeomorphism class of the stable set a complete set of topological invariants for discrete holomorphic local dynamical systems in End(C, O) having a Cremer point at the origin?

accepted.question_text: Given two one-variable germs tangent to the identity, is there an effective decision procedure for determining whether they are holomorphically locally conjugate, despite the impracticality of explicitly computing the full Écalle-Voronin functional invariants in general?

evidence.quote: (OP4) Give an effective procedure for deciding whether two germs tangent to the identity are holomorphically locally conjugated.

accepted.question_text: Given two one-variable parabolic germs, is there an effective decision procedure for determining whether they are holomorphically locally conjugate, taking into account the multiplier, parabolic multiplicity, iterative residue, and the usually intractable functional invariants that complete the holomorphic classification?

evidence.quote: (OP4′) Give an effective procedure for deciding whether two parabolic germs are holomorphically locally conjugated.

accepted.question_text: Let f be a non-invertible dominant holomorphic germ in End(C^n, O), and let c_∞(f)=lim_{k→∞} c(f^k)^{1/k} be its asymptotic attraction rate, where c(f) is the order of f. Must c_∞(f) always be an algebraic integer of degree at most n? More precisely, do there exist integers a_0, ..., a_{n-1} with c_∞^n + a_{n-1} c_∞^{n-1} + ... + a_0 = 0, and does there also exist δ in (0,1] such that δ c_∞^k ≤ c(f^k) ≤ c_∞^k for all k≥1?

evidence.quote: (OP5) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be non-invertible and dominant. Is it true that c∞ = c∞(f) is an algebraic integer of order at most n ... ? Moreover, does there exist δ ∈ (0, 1] such that δc∞^k ≤ c(f^k) ≤ c∞^k for all k ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^n, O), does the sequence of orders of its iterates, {c(f^k)}_{k∈N}, eventually satisfy a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: (OP6) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be non-invertible and dominant. Is it true that the sequence {c(f^k)}k∈N satisfies, at least for k large enough, a linear recursion formula with integer coefficients?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n, O), and let H be the first nonzero homogeneous term in its expansion. If H is degenerate, meaning H(v)=0 for some nonzero v, and if the postcritical set of f is an analytic cone near the origin, must f nevertheless be holomorphically locally conjugate to H?

evidence.quote: (OP7) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be a superattracting germ ... Assume that H is degenerate ... Is it still true that if the postcritical set of f is an analytic cone then f is holomorphically locally conjugated to H?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n, O) with first nonzero homogeneous term H, and suppose the postcritical set of f is a topological cone near the origin. Under what additional conditions is f topologically locally conjugate to H? In particular, is the answer always yes when H is non-degenerate?

evidence.quote: (OP8) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be a superattracting germ ... Assume that the postcritical set of f is a topological cone nearby the origin. Under which conditions is then f topologically locally conjugated to H? In particular, is this true when H is non-degenerate?

accepted.question_text: Let f and g be superattracting germs in End(C^n, O) of the same order. Is local topological or holomorphic conjugacy between f and g completely determined by the corresponding conjugacy type of their postcritical sets? Equivalently, does a local homeomorphism or biholomorphism sending PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g) suffice, together with equality of order, to characterize local conjugacy?

evidence.quote: (OP9) Let f, g ∈ End(C^n, O) be two superattracting germs, with c(f) = c(g). Is it true that f and g are topologically (respectively, holomorphically) locally conjugated if and only if their postcritical sets are topologically (respectively, holomorphically) conjugated...?

accepted.question_text: Determine formal normal forms and complete formal-conjugacy invariants for superattracting germs of order 2 in End(C^n, O) when n≥3, and for superattracting germs of order 3 in End(C^2, O).

evidence.quote: (OP10) Classify with respect to formal conjugation the superattracting germs f ∈ End(C^n, O) of order 2 when n ≥ 3, or of order 3 when n = 2.

accepted.question_text: Classify 3-dimensional non-invertible dominant rigid holomorphic germs, in the sense of giving normal forms or complete invariants for their birational-dynamical classification.

evidence.quote: (OP11) Classify 3-dimensional non-invertible dominant rigid germs.

accepted.question_text: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^3, O), under what conditions does there exist a modification π: M̃ → C^3 based at the origin, a point p in the exceptional fiber π^{-1}(O), and a holomorphic germ f̃ in End(M̃, p) that is rigid or at least weakly rigid and satisfies π ◦ f̃ = f ◦ π?

evidence.quote: (OP12) Under which conditions on f ∈ End(C^3, O) there exist a modification π: M˜ → C^3 based at O, a point p ∈ E = π^{-1}(O) and a (possibly weakly) rigid holomorphic germ f˜ ∈ End(M˜, p) so that π ◦ f˜ = f ◦ π?

accepted.question_text: Is every germ f in End(C^n, O) that is tangent to the identity and has the origin as an isolated fixed point guaranteed to admit at least one Fatou flower tangent to some characteristic direction, even in dimensions n≥3 where all characteristic directions may be degenerate?

evidence.quote: (OP13) Is it true that every germ f ∈ End(C^n, O) tangent to the identity, with the origin as an isolated fixed point, admits at least one Fatou flower tangent to some direction?

accepted.question_text: For a germ tangent to the identity in C^n, describe its stable set in terms of characteristic directions, directors, indices, and any additional necessary invariants. In particular, determine how those data control which points converge to the origin, including phenomena not captured merely by convergence tangent to a characteristic direction.

evidence.quote: (OP14) Describe, using characteristic directions, directors, indices and possibly other invariants, the stable set of a germ tangent to the identity in C^n.

accepted.question_text: Let f be a germ in End(C^n, O) of the form f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+O(∥z∥^{ν+1}), where P_ν is homogeneous of degree ν and every characteristic direction of f is non-degenerate. Must f be topologically locally conjugate to the time-1 map of the homogeneous vector field P_ν?
accepted.context_brief: Topological normal forms via homogeneous flows

evidence.quote: (OP15) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be given by f(z) = z + Pν(z) + O(kzk^{ν+1}), and assume that all characteristic directions of f are non-degenerate. Is it true that f is topologically locally conjugated to the time-1 map of the homogeneous vector field Pν?

accepted.question_text: Find formal normal forms and complete formal invariants for germs tangent to the identity whose characteristic directions are all degenerate. This asks for the missing part of the formal classification beyond the case where at least one non-degenerate characteristic direction is present.
accepted.context_brief: Formal classification with only degenerate directions

evidence.quote: (OP15) Find formal normal forms and invariants for germs tangent to the identity having only degenerate characteristic directions.

accepted.question_text: Consider the geodesic field G = g_1(z) v ∂/∂z + (ν−1) g_2(z) v^2 ∂/∂v arising from a homogeneous vector field in dimension two. What is the local dynamical behavior of G near an irregular singularity (ζ_0, 0), where the vanishing orders satisfy μ_1(ζ_0) > μ_2(ζ_0) + 1?

evidence.quote: (OP16) Describe the local dynamics of a vector field G of the form (5) about an irregular singularity (ζ0, 0).

accepted.question_text: Let λ⃗=(λ_1,...,λ_n) be eigenvalues for a diagonalizable differential, and suppose the Brjuno-type series Σ_{k≥0} 2^{-k} log(1/Ω_{λ⃗}(2^{k+1})) diverges. Does there then exist a formally linearizable germ f in End(C^n, O) with those eigenvalues that fails to be holomorphically linearizable?

evidence.quote: (OP17) Let ~λ = (λ1, . . . , λn) ∈ C^n be such that Σ ... = +∞. Is it possible to find f ∈ End(C^n, O), with diagonalizable differential having eigenvalues λ1, . . . , λn, which is formally linearizable but not holomorphically linearizable?

accepted.question_text: Given eigenvalues λ⃗=(λ_1,...,λ_n), construct families {f_{λ⃗,a}}_{a∈M} of formally linearizable germs in End(C^n, O) with diagonal differential diag(λ_1,...,λ_n) such that holomorphic linearizability holds exactly when λ⃗ satisfies the several-variable Brjuno condition (8). In particular, for n=2 and nonresonant (λ_1,λ_2), is every germ of the form f(z)=(λ_1 z_1, λ_2 z_2)+Q(z) with Q quadratic homogeneous holomorphically linearizable if and only if (λ_1,λ_2) satisfies (8)?

evidence.quote: (OP18) Given ~λ = (λ1, . . . , λn) ∈ C^n, find families {f~λ,a}a∈M ⊂ End(C^n, O) ... such that f~λ,a is holomorphically linearizable if and only if ~λ satisfies (8). For instance, is it true that a germ of the form f(z) = (λ1z1, λ2z2)+Q(z) ... is holomorphically linearizable if and only if (λ1, λ2) satisfy (8)?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the arXiv PDF 1107.4876 and mapped the paper structure. Open-question regions were identified in the introduction (Q1-Q5), Section 2 (OP1-OP4′), and Section 3 (OP5-OP18).
Extracted the five explicit general questions Q1-Q5 from the introduction as open classification and dynamics questions.
Extracted explicit one-variable open problems OP1, OP2, OP3, OP4, and OP4′ from Sections 2.1-2.4.
Extracted explicit several-variable open problems OP5-OP18 from Sections 3.1-3.7, including the duplicated OP15 labels in the source.

Rewrote each explicit question into self-contained form by expanding notation such as stable sets, postcritical sets, asymptotic attraction rate, characteristic directions, and Brjuno-type conditions using surrounding source text only.
No near-duplicate questions were merged. The source uses the label OP15 twice for distinct problems; both were preserved as separate accepted items q_021 and q_022.
All accepted items have explicit source-backed question statements with page-level evidence and were expanded without introducing unsupported facts.
